explanation: The old ball measured 38 mm. The switch came after the Sydney Olympics: a bigger ball meets more air resistance, so rallies run a little slower and are easier to follow on television.

claims.text: The table tennis ball adopted for official play in 2000 has a diameter of 40 mm.
The ball adopted in 2000 is not 32 mm, 35 mm or 38 mm across.
Before the change, the official table tennis ball measured 38 mm across.
The International Table Tennis Federation brought in the 40 mm ball in October 2000, after the Sydney Olympic Games.
The larger ball was adopted to slow the game slightly and make rallies easier for spectators and television viewers to follow.

stem: In 2000, table tennis adopted a new official ball. What diameter is that ball?

evidence.restatement: Official table tennis balls have been 40 mm across since the ITTF changed the standard from the earlier smaller size in 2000.

claimResults.note: Rival test: 38 mm is the pre-2000 size and the only distractor with real pull, but the stem fixes the new ball. The 2014 plastic ball is also 40 mm, so no second answer. High-risk number: confirmed directly (memo 18). One web search on the ITTF change gave 1 October 2000 effective, but the summary cited no single result and mixed in blogs, so I do not cite it as evidence.

evidence.restatement: No official ball was ever 32 mm or 35 mm; the 2000 change went from 38 mm up to 40 mm.

claimResults.note: 38 mm is the previous size, so it is wrong for the ball adopted in 2000.

evidence.restatement: The standard ball before the ITTF's 2000 rule change was the 38 mm ball.

claimResults.note: Agrees with the search summary (38 mm to 40 mm).

evidence.restatement: The ITTF's larger ball took effect on 1 October 2000, the day the Sydney Games closed.

claimResults.note: Sydney ran 15 September to 1 October 2000, so 'after' the Games is fair. The search summary also gave 1 October 2000.

evidence.restatement: The ITTF's stated reason was that a bigger ball is slowed more by air and spins less, giving longer rallies that television viewers can follow.

claimResults.note: Widely documented rationale; the search summary agreed.

issues.note: The 2014 move to plastic 40+ balls could make a pedant ask which new ball, but the stem says 2000 and both are 40 mm, so the key holds.
